description:
Decided in 'How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?' (defk-dtw.16): speed comes from everything that keeps Elixir's answer; protection of the BEAM also uses C's own hardening. Measure -fstack-protector-strong, -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 and -fno-strict-overflow across the catalog; adopt in normal builds if the cost is under 2%, otherwise record the cost and decision. Part of the evidence for the runtime threat list (defk-5fc).

Done when the flags are adopted or rejected with the measurement recorded.

comments.text:
Measurement 2026-10-08 (M-series Mac, Apple clang 17, macOS 26.7.1): 7 interleaved rounds (4 + 3) against the unflagged baseline, variant order rotated each round, best-of per round, per README harness conventions (sum/dot best-of-7 over 5M f64; count_primes(_early) best-of-3 over 1M). Deltas merged across both runs (min of mins):

  variant                    sum       dot      primes     early     worst
  +fstack-protector-strong  +0.42%    +0.98%    +0.40%    +0.41%    +0.98%
  +_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2        +0.17%    +0.16%    -0.24%    -0.26%    +0.17%
  +fno-strict-overflow      +0.72%    -0.13%    +0.23%    +1.62%    +1.62%
  all three                 +0.72%    +0.33%    +0.59%    +1.64%    +1.64%

Noise band: README documents +/-3% code-layout noise (defk-wnu); the round-1 fortify dot outlier (+2.65% in the first 4 rounds) disappeared in rounds 5-7 (+0.16%), confirming layout noise not a flag effect.

Decision: ADOPT all three (worst metric +1.64% < 2% bar). lib/defk/build.ex @cflags updated with a comment citing this measurement; mix test 156 passed with the flags active. Note: an earlier session left a contradictory edit claiming fno-strict-overflow rejected at +2.4%/+4.3% — not reproduced by this interleaved measurement; discarded.

title: Measure hardening flags for kernel builds
